PullRequest.Title: Agents window: close a chat's canvases as it leaves a chat window, and fix the chat window's Changes tabs
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-ups to #346752 for chat windows in the Agents window. No issue was filed: the user decided these while reviewing #346752.

## Bugs

1. **A canvas shows an error after its chat leaves a chat window.** A chat window shows chats A and B, and B's canvas is open in the window's editor part. When B's tab is closed or moved out, the canvas stays. Once it shows again it displays the "Canvases can only be shown…" error pane.
2. **The chat window's Changes entry shows another chat's changes.** The entry activated any Changes tab of the window's session. That could be another chat's tab, or a session-level tab whose diffs don't follow the shown chat.
3. **Changes tabs can't be told apart.** Since #346752 a chat window can show Changes tabs of several chats of a session, and they were all titled "Changes".

## Causes

1. `CanvasService` never re-checked whether a group can still present a canvas that is already open in it. `SessionCanvasContextService.canPresentInGroup` read the chat window's chats once, without tracking them.
2. The entry matched Changes tabs by session (`getSessionResource`) rather than by the chat the window shows.
3. `SessionChangesEditorInput` had no description, and its title didn't name the chat.

## Changes

- **Canvases (O29).**
  - `ICanvasContextService.canPresentInGroup` and `canPresentCanvasInGroup` take an optional reader. The Sessions implementation reads the chat windows and their chats with it.
  - `CanvasService` closes an open canvas once a group that shows it can no longer present it. It re-checks as presentations change and as a canvas opens in a group, including one the user moved it to.
  - The close records no dismissal, so the canvas shows again beside its chat wherever that chat shows next. It isn't suspended for a working-set restore, which would reopen it in the main window.
  - A canvas that another surface shows, such as a pinned canvas page, keeps its presentation and model there, as when the user closes its editor.
  - Groups of the main window always present canvases, so the main window is unchanged.
- **Changes entry (O31).** The entry activates the Changes tab of the chat the window shows, matched by its exact resource. Otherwise it opens one for that chat.
- **Changes tab titles.** The Changes editor of a chat has the chat's title as its description, and the Changes editor of a session has "Session", as in the Changes header's "Session · N Files". Tabs show descriptions only when several share the name "Changes", so a Changes tab on its own still reads "Changes". The title and accessible label of a chat's Changes editor read "Changes · <chat title>", and they follow the chat as it is renamed. A session's keep their plain "Changes".

## Known issues

- A session-level Changes tab, such as one restored from before #346752, is no longer reused while the window shows a chat. It stays open as its own tab, and the entry opens the shown chat's Changes. Its diffs follow the chat the main window shows for the session, so reusing it could show the wrong chat's changes.
- A chat window's canvases don't come back after a window reload. Canvas inputs restore only during a main window working-set restore, and canvases reopen only for the chat of the focused window. This is unchanged here.

## Validation

Each new test failed before its fix, then passed.

- `./scripts/test.sh` on the canvas, session canvas, chat window and sessions suites: 633 passing, 2 pending (existing `test.skip`).
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium` on the browser suites among them: 494 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh` on the Changes, editor, chat window and session changes suites: 268 passing; `node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium` on them: 267 passing.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` (with `set -o pipefail`): passed.
- `pnpm run eslint` on the changed files: passed.
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed.

Live in a Code OSS dev build of the Agents window, with a real agent session and a test canvas:
- A chat window showed chats A and B, each with its canvas open in the window's editor part. Closing B's tab closed B's canvas and kept A's, with no error pane in either window, and the main window's editors were unchanged.
- Showing B in the window again reopened its canvas in the chat window.
- With a session-level Changes tab already open, the entry opened A's Changes, then B's Changes, then activated A's existing tab again.
- A canvas opened in the main window and then moved into the chat window showing its chat closed once that chat's tab closed, with no error pane, and the main window was unchanged.
- The tab strip showed a single Changes tab of a chat, or of the session, as plain "Changes"; the session's tab beside a chat's as "Changes  Session" and "Changes  Create a.txt"; and two chats' tabs as "Changes  Create a.txt" and "Changes  Create b.txt". Each chat's Changes tab kept its own diffs as the active chat switched; clicking another chat's tab switched and closed nothing; after a window reload all three tabs restored with their chats.
- Both chats' canvases stayed open as tabs whichever chat was active, and clicking either showed it without an error pane.

Not verified live: a canvas also shown on a pinned canvas page; unit tests cover it.

Scenarios.Scenario: A chat tab leaves a chat window while one or more of that chat's canvas editors are open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The chat-window chats observable invalidates the new canvas autorun; it synchronously checks tracked canvas inputs and starts closeInput for disallowed groups. Editor closing and browser-view destruction are not awaited by the chat-removal operation, so cleanup is off that interaction's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Destroy the external BrowserView backing a canvas model via BrowserViewModel.dispose -> destroyBrowserView.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one destroy request for each invalid open canvas that has a resolved model; C requests when all C such canvases leave.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The canvas editor and its model remained open after the chat left, so this cleanup boundary was not reached on this event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget cleanup; it does not block the chat tab leaving, though many models can create a cleanup burst.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number C of currently tracked/open canvas inputs, across visible and retained working sets; invalid cleanup cardinality is the subset belonging to chats that left the window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The autorun checks inputs serially. Invalid inputs start independent async closeInput operations without a shared limiter; model disposal synchronously initiates one fire-and-forget destroy request per resolved canvas model.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Inputs without a resolved browser model avoid browser-view destruction; each invalid input is synchronously removed from the maps before asynchronous editor closure, preventing repeat cleanup of the same input.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the observable dependency, per-input iteration, close path, and BrowserView destruction call are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The live canvas collection is provider-supplied and has no explicit cap, but repository scenarios and tests establish only small numbers of simultaneously open canvases. No evidence shows a realistic count large enough for the required off-path cleanup burst to regress responsiveness.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added work releases heavyweight browser resources that previously remained live, is proportional to resources that must be cleaned up, and runs off the chat-removal critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: A canvas editor opens or is moved between main-window and chat-window editor groups
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An EDITOR_OPEN event and presentation-state signals run the new synchronous validation before subsequent UI work; actual BrowserView creation and URL loading remain on the existing canvas-resolution path and were not moved by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an external BrowserView for a canvas and load its URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One creation/load per canvas model cache miss; reused presentations avoid creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create/load occurred when a canvas model first resolved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for first canvas rendering and unchanged by this PR; the new group validation itself performs no IPC/network operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: C tracked canvas inputs, G editor groups, and E open editors. Each validation pass calls findEditors for each non-opening input; lookup uses a resource counter fast check and then scans groups containing matching resources.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Validation is synchronous and serial. Existing canvas opens and BrowserView creation can already proceed concurrently; the diff does not add concurrency to those boundaries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: EditorService uses EditorsObserver.hasEditors as a resource-presence fast path. No new cache is introduced; validation reacts only to canvas opens, presentation lifecycle signals, and relevant chat-window observables rather than render, scroll, or input frames.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous scan and its scaling; low for any user-visible degradation at realistic cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The new scan is multiplicative in open canvases and editors, but it runs on lifecycle events rather than a hot frame/input path, and no realistic high-cardinality restore/open case is established by the repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The scan is newly added repeated CPU work, but available evidence does not establish a concrete, realistic latency regression rather than a bounded lifecycle check.

Scenarios.Scenario: The Changes entry is invoked in a chat window with or without an exact chat-scoped Changes tab
Scenarios.CriticalPath: If the exact resource is already open, the command only scans the group's editor list and activates it. Otherwise it opens a chat-scoped SessionChangesEditorInput; resolving that active editor builds the multi-diff resource list and resolves text models before the view is ready.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve original and modified text models for each changed file through ITextModelService while opening a new chat-scoped multi-diff editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 2F model-reference resolutions for F changed files, with model-service reuse where available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Any Changes tab resolving to the same session could be activated, avoiding a new resolve but potentially showing another chat's changes; when no session tab existed, the same open/resolve path already ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the critical path to rendering a newly opened Changes editor. For a window that only has a session-level or another chat's tab, the stricter match can newly take this path instead of activating the wrong tab.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: E editors in the target group for exact-resource matching; on a miss, F changed files in the selected chat, with up to two text-model references per file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The editor match is serial. MultiDiff model resolution uses paired Promise.allSettled calls per file and the existing multi-diff machinery; the diff adds no limiter or scheduling change inside that machinery.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An already-open exact chat resource is reused. MultiDiff inputs lazily create their inner input, and when a Changes editor stops being shown its view model is cleared unless another group shows the same input. Different chat resources intentionally do not share models because their change sets differ.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the miss path and per-file model resolution; high that the changed matching can cause a new open where a non-exact session tab exists.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: File count and model cache warmth vary. The newly reached work is tied to the intentional requirement for a distinct authoritative chat change set, and inactive replaced Changes inputs release their view models, so no unbounded retained-model growth is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The additional resolve is necessary to avoid presenting a different chat's data, exact resources are reused thereafter, and repository cleanup releases inactive view models; there is no bounded alternative proven that preserves the required semantics while eliminating the work.

Scenarios.Scenario: A chat-scoped Changes tab is created, displayed, or updated after a chat rename/session change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction parses the resource twice, subscribes one derived title observer, and computes the matching chat title. A rename/session event recomputes the session lookup and scans that session's chats before firing a label update; no external operation blocks tab display.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: T open chat-scoped Changes inputs and H chats in each associated session; a global session-change event can cause O(T*H) in-memory URI comparisons.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All observer recomputation is synchronous and serial on the event dispatch. There is no queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The derived observable caches/comparatively propagates its string value, and each listener is disposed with its editor input. Session-level Changes inputs use a constant observable and do not subscribe.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for listener lifetime and O(T*H) recomputation; low for material performance impact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Many simultaneous chat-scoped Changes tabs are possible, but normal editor cardinality is small and session-change events are lifecycle/provider updates rather than per-frame events. No evidence establishes enough T or H to cause visible label-update latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The work is bounded to live editor inputs, disposed correctly, and no realistic hot-path or boundary amplification is demonstrated.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and relevant canvas, editor, BrowserView, session-management, and multi-diff call paths. The diff adds lifecycle-time canvas validation and required cleanup, plus exact chat Changes matching and reactive labels. No actionable, high-confidence performance regression was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
